verdicts.evidence: src/TreeHash.jl:47 changed `isempty(_nonempty(path, skip)) && continue` to `_nonempty(path, skip) || continue`, exactly the hint's fix. Verified live: `julia` run of `TreeHash.tree_hash` over a dir containing only an empty subdirectory now returns `4b825dc642cb6eb9a060e54bf8d69288fbee4904`, git's canonical empty-tree id (matches `git init && git add -A && git write-tree` on the same tree), where pre-fix it wrongly included the empty subdir. New test/treehash.jl compares against real `git write-tree` on a mixed tree (file + non-empty subdir + nested-empty subdir) and against the canonical empty-tree id for an all-empty tree; both assertions pass (`julia --project=. test/treehash.jl` -> 2/2 pass).

verdicts.question: implementation
verdicts.evidence: src/Witnesses.jl:170 now requires `f == 0 && blocked !== nothing` before returning :blocked in the `e > 0` (TestSetException) branch, exactly per the hint; test/witnesses.jl's new `blocked_but_failed.jl` (a failing @test plus an erroring @test under a `# blocked:` header) is classified :broken with reason naming both counts, and `julia --project=. test/witnesses.jl` passes 12/12. But the sibling `m === nothing` branch at line 164 (`blocked === nothing || return WitnessResult(name, :blocked, 0, 0, 0, blocked)`) was untouched and carries the identical class: it returns :blocked purely from `blocked !== nothing`, hardcoding fail=0 without checking whether the witness actually failed first. I reproduced this live: a witness with `# blocked:` header containing `@test 1 == 2` (a real failing assertion, NOT wrapped to catch it as an Error) followed by a bare `error("boom")` outside any @test hits this exact branch (Julia's raw exception here is not a TestSetException, so `m === nothing`), and `run_one` returned `WitnessResult("probe.jl", :blocked, 0, 0, 1, "probe")` — classified BLOCKED with the fail silently dropped to 0, contradicting the same 'errored, failed nothing' docstring claim (Witnesses.jl:32-33, 145-148) the finding cites. The fix pass addressed only the `e > 0` branch's instance, not this second branch carrying the same defect class.

class_surfaces.evidence: the flagged e>0/TestSetException branch now gates on f == 0 before returning :blocked; verified by the new test/witnesses.jl case (blocked_but_failed.jl -> :broken, reason mentions '1 assertion(s) failed').

the m === nothing (raw, non-TestSetException) branch still returns :blocked solely from `blocked !== nothing`, with fail hardcoded to 0 regardless of any assertion that actually failed before the raw exception. Live repro: a `# blocked:` witness with `@test 1 == 2` (fails) then a bare `error("boom")` (not wrapped in @test) produced `WitnessResult("probe.jl", :blocked, 0, 0, 1, "probe")` under the fixed code — the genuine failure is silently dropped, contradicting the same 'was never seen to fail' / 'failed nothing' docstring claim this finding is about.
